programme: An FGF2→EGR1 growth-factor/immediate-early-gene induction axis, with HDAC1 setting the chromatin/PTM state that gates whether EGR1-dependent transcription proceeds
role_in_a: In colorectal epithelium, FGF2 signaling is measured as a proliferative/biomarker axis (41660908) while an EGR1-linked circuit (SCAMP2-EGR1) suppresses tumour growth (42547420); HDAC1 sits downstream, its post-translational state (CDK1 decrotonylation) restraining proliferation (42382394) and its modulation determining sensitivity to HDAC-inhibitor cytotoxicity (42455377) — i.e. the module sets proliferative/survival balance in the tumour cell.
role_in_b: In Parkinson's models the same three nodes recur as a stress-adaptive, neuroprotective circuit: astrocyte-derived FGF2 protects synapses and mitochondria (40248029) and supports autophagy over apoptosis (34459097); EGR1 is repressed under oxidative stress and its restoration is neuroprotective (37166273), with an EGR1-midnolin link affecting neurite outgrowth (39264361); HDAC1-linked epigenetic modulation is protective across several PD models (41936814, 38458535, 40176114) — the module here supports neuronal survival under stress rather than proliferation.
shared_axis: A transforming colon epithelial cell and a stressed dopaminergic neuron both appear to reuse the same growth-factor-to-immediate-early-gene wiring (FGF2 → EGR1, chromatin-gated by HDAC1) to reprogram transcription under stress; the direction of the output differs by tissue — growth/survival advantage in the tumour, cytoprotection in the neuron — but the circuit topology is the same.
reasoning: All three carrying factors are independently and specifically documented in both diseases by the retrieved papers, not merely in one — that clears the bar for 'strong'. The FGF-immediate-early-gene-to-chromatin wiring is a recognisable, nameable module in its own right, so the programme does not depend on speculative target-list inference. What is not in the record is any paper connecting the two diseases through this axis directly, so the cross-disease link itself rests on reasoning about shared circuitry rather than a stated fact — hence 'supported', not 'established'.
support: 41660908 — FGF2 expression evaluated as a CRC biomarker; 42547420 — SCAMP2-EGR1 axis suppresses CRC cell growth; 42382394 — HDAC1-mediated CDK1 decrotonylation restrains CRC proliferation; 42455377 — HDAC1 modulation determines panobinostat cytotoxicity in CRC; 40248029 — FGF2-primed astrocyte vesicles protect against mitochondrial/synaptic toxicity in PD models; 34459097 — FGF2-linked miR-497-5p pathway shifts apoptosis/autophagy balance in PD models; 37166273 — miR-381 represses EGR1 and this alleviates oxidative stress in PD models; 39264361 — midnolin (PD risk gene) promotes neurite outgrowth via EGR1; 41936814 — valsartan neuroprotection via epigenetic/HDAC modulation in PD; 38458535 — HDAC1 flagged in a PD pathogenesis gene network; 40176114 — HDAC-linked endothelial pathway ameliorates blood-brain-barrier dysfunction in a stress/cognitive-decline model relevant to PD.
how_to_falsify: Stimulate a CRC organoid line and an FGF2-primed astrocyte/iPSC-dopaminergic-neuron co-culture in parallel with FGF2, then knock down EGR1 in both; if EGR1 loss changes CRC proliferation but leaves neuronal survival/oxidative-stress resistance unaffected (or vice versa), the claim of a shared circuit fails. A complementary test: ChIP-seq for HDAC1 occupancy at EGR1 target promoters in a CRC line versus a stressed dopaminergic neuron line under FGF2 stimulation — substantially divergent occupancy would undercut the shared-wiring claim.
caveats: Blood|colorectal tissue pairing over 171 patient-group comparisons but only 4 independent cohort pairs, so replication is thinner than the comparison count suggests. GLI1, the canonical Hedgehog master regulator, was removed as tissue-generic — this is why a more obvious-looking 'enteric nervous system / gut-brain axis' story built on HAND2, GLI3, SOX5, HOXD3 and IRX3 was not used: those factors lack disease-specific documentation individually and their most recognisable pathway partner is background signal for this tissue pair, not disease signal. KLF17 (CRC tumour-suppressor evidence only) targets PARK7/DJ-1, a canonical PD gene — a suggestive but entirely untested link, not evidence, and not used to support the verdict. ZGPAT, HOXD3, IRX3 and SOX5 have no disease-specific literature in either disease and are excluded from the programme for that reason. Single-view factors (LHX9, ARID4A, KMT2C, DMRTA1, FOSB, NPM1, PRDM16, RCOR1, ZNF135) were excluded as required.
